best_for: Retro gamers who want one program for many emulators, with CRT shaders, netplay and achievements, and who bring their own game files.

points.title: One front end, many cores
points.text: RetroArch runs emulators and game engines as cores, and the project counts over 200. Settings, controls and menus stay the same whichever system you play.

points.title: Extras built in
points.text: Shaders mimic CRT screens, a netplay lobby lets you host or join online games with spectators, run-ahead cuts input lag, and achievements, recording and streaming are included.

points.title: Bring your own games
points.text: RetroArch plays content you supply, such as your own discs, and some cores need the original game's data files to work.

points.title: Skip the Steam build for full control
points.text: The Steam version has no core updater or thumbnail scraping, and only a set of cores from Steam itself. The project recommends the desktop download for the full feature set.

points.title: Old computers still covered
points.text: Current Windows builds run on Windows 7 to 11, with separate legacy builds back to Windows 95. Modern Macs need macOS 10.13 or later; there are older builds for Intel Macs and PowerPC.

points.title: Versions kept
points.text: RetroArch is free under GPL-3.0. The Windows listing keeps 15 versions, with 32-bit and 64-bit installers for all users. macOS and Linux list only the current release; the Flatpak is marked verified by Flathub.
